name: the semantic path minimises total distance, then hops, then walks back by ID
why: Weights are 1 - cosine similarity. Three two-hop routes from a to d each cost exactly 1 (0.5+0.5, 0.25+0.75, 0.625+0.375, all exact in binary), the direct link costs 1.5, and a zero-weight link from d to f makes a three-hop route of equal cost.

queries.why: The direct link (1.5) loses on cost. Routes through b, c, e and f all cost 1 in 2 hops; walking back from d, b is the smallest neighbour on such a route.
a-f costs 1 in one hop; a-b-d-f also costs 1 but in three. Equal cost prefers fewer hops.
Direction is ignored. Walking back from a, b is the smallest neighbour one hop closer at matching cost.
Counting hops instead of weight, the direct link wins.
